key_insight: A multi-branch shell model shows stronger intermittency than the standard Sabra model, indicating that both nonlinear interactions and branching geometry are important for turbulent cascades.
engineering_relevance: For reduced-order turbulence modeling, the result suggests that capturing cascade structure requires not just local dynamics but also the growth of active degrees of freedom across scales.
method: Built a multi-branch shell model with quasi-local triadic nonlinear couplings
Compared its scaling behavior against the standard Sabra shell model
Analyzed multiplier statistics and large-deviation properties of the cascade
evidence_signal: The abstract reports anomalous scaling exponents of energy-flux structure functions and multiplier statistics as the main evaluation signals, with branching producing enhanced intermittency.
watch_item: Because this is a reduced shell model, its conclusions may not transfer directly to full Navier-Stokes flows without careful validation.
paper_title: Intermittency in Shell Models of Turbulent Cascades: from Single-Branch to Multi-Branch
